analysis.title: UBS House View Monthly Extended December 2026
key_insights: UBS CIO downgraded global equities, the US, Switzerland, the UK, Asia ex-Japan, EM, Australia, Taiwan and Japan to Neutral. Europe, the Eurozone, China A-shares, India and Singapore stay Attractive. The downgrade reflects a more balanced risk-reward, not a bearish outlook.

Fixed income is rated Attractive across high grade, investment grade, high yield and EM bonds. Gold and silver were upgraded to Attractive alongside copper. Oil is Neutral. Cash is the least preferred asset class.

Scenario probabilities for December 2027: Goldilocks 20%, Resilience (base) 50%, Yield reset 10%, AI bust 20%. Base-case targets: MSCI ACWI 1,460 (+8%), S&P 500 8,200 (+8%), EuroStoxx 50 7,000 (+9%), US 10y yield 4.75%, Fed funds upper bound 4.50%, gold USD 4,400/oz.

US equities cut from Attractive to Neutral. The 10 largest companies are just under 40% of the S&P 500. S&P 500 EPS estimates raised to USD 360 in 2026 (+29%) and USD 415 in 2027 (+15%). The June 2027 S&P target was lowered to 8,000 from 8,400 and a December 2027 target of 8,200 was introduced. Financials were cut to Neutral and energy to Unattractive.

AI investment is expected to rise from about USD 1.0tr in 2026 to USD 1.4tr in 2027. The key uncertainty is shifting to 2028 (financing, monetization, power and grid constraints). UBS favors quality within AI and AI-resilient quality stocks, and estimates AI revenues at a run rate below USD 200bn today.

The Eurozone stays Attractive and Preferred. 2026 Eurozone earnings growth was raised to 20% from 15%, 2027 stays at 15%, and 2028 is introduced at 8%. The June 2027 Euro Stoxx 50 target was cut to 6,800 from 7,100 on higher bond yields. European utilities were upgraded to Attractive and European consumer discretionary cut to Neutral. Cyclicals have underperformed defensives by about 17% since mid-June.

UK equities were cut to Neutral and are Least Preferred. 2026 UK earnings growth was raised to 24% from 16%, with energy contributing 14-15pp. Growth is forecast to slow to 6% in 2027 and 4% in 2028. Swiss equities are Neutral and Least Preferred, with SMI profit growth of 11% in 2026 and 8% in 2027.

Asia ex-Japan, EM, Taiwan and Japan were cut to Neutral over AI capex digestion risk and reduced visibility beyond 2027. MSCI Asia ex-Japan and EM earnings are forecast to grow 72% and 63% in 2026, and 20% in 2027. Asia ex-Japan and EM trade at 8.0x forward P/E. China A-shares are preferred over H-shares. Topix is down 6% in the past month and up 16% YTD, with a 12% earnings growth forecast for FY26 and 10% for FY27.

Australian equities were cut to Neutral. House prices fell 1.2% m/m in October and are down about 6.7% from the March 2026 peak. The RBA hiked to an 18-year high cash rate. UBS expects a 2-3 quarter lagged hit to consumption and the labor market and sees downside risk to bank earnings.

US 10y Treasury yield hit a cycle high of 5.36% in early October, then fell toward 4.8%. UBS expects an equilibrium range of 4.5-5.0%. October CPI came in hotter than expected at 3.7% y/y after Waller's speech opening the door to a 50bp hike. Markets price roughly 75bps more tightening by mid-2027 and UBS thinks this is too hawkish. UBS expects 25bp Fed hikes in December and March, with rates staying at 4.25-4.50% through 2027.

UBS prefers the 2- to 5-year Treasury segment, with a selective extension toward 10 years for diversification. Five-year US yields would need to rise 113bps for capital losses to offset a year of income. Eurozone 10y Bund yields likely peaked in late September near 3.5%. The ECB held in October.

US IG spreads are 91bps against a median of 129bps since 2010, and yields are 5.99% (US) and 4.26% (EUR). Hyperscalers are about 4.7% of the US IG index, and AI-related bonds trade about 68bps wider than comparable IG. US HY spreads are around 330-340bps, about 100bps wider than the summer lows. CCC spreads are above 1,000bps. HY defaults are 1.8% (US) and 1.3% (EUR), with about 2% expected over 12 months. UBS targets 300bps for both HY markets in December 2027.

EM bonds are Attractive and Preferred, with sovereign and corporate yields of 7.3% and 7.1% and EMBI up 1.4% in October. Asia credit is Attractive: JACI IG yields 6.0% at 82bps, and Asia HY yields 8.0% at 304bps.

UBS expects USD support near term and now sees EURUSD broadly sideways into early 2027, with weakness returning later: DXY below 100 and EURUSD above 1.15 later in 2027 after the French elections. GBP, SEK and CNY are Attractive. AUD and NZD were cut to Unattractive, NOK to Neutral and SEK raised to Attractive. CHF is a funding currency. MXN, BRL, ZAR and INR carry is favored. CNY is expected to gain 3.0-3.5% in 2027. JPY stays Neutral.

Gold was upgraded to Attractive with a December 2027 target of USD 5,000/oz. It hit nearly USD 5,600 early in 2026 and now trades around USD 3,885 under high real yields and a firm dollar. UBS says it could stay below USD 4,000 in the near term. Forward curve is near USD 3,900, vol is about 25%, and UBS suggests selling gold volatility as an indirect way to express the view. Base-case Brent is USD 90 in June 2027 and USD 80 in December 2027, versus about USD 92 now. Copper is the preferred industrial metal.

Macro: US 3Q GDP grew 3.4% annualized. Core CPI 3m annualized is 3.7% and core PCE tracks 3.2% y/y. AI capex added about 0.6pp to growth YTD. Eurozone GDP is forecast at 1.1% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027, with headline inflation reaching 4.3% by early 2027 and two more ECB hikes (December, March). SNB hikes are expected in March and June 2027 to 0.5%. China 2027 GDP is mid-4% after 4.6% in 2026, with October PPI at 5.7% y/y.

Alternatives: equity market neutral, merger arbitrage, fixed income relative value and discretionary macro hedge funds are Attractive. Private equity buyouts, growth equity, secondaries and infrastructure are Attractive. Real estate was cut to Neutral. UBS recommends putting surplus cash to work and using cash, concentrated tech and single-stock positions, and US energy as funding sources.

sector_views.rationale: Consumer spending should stay resilient and energy price volatility is manageable unless prices spike to new highs.
No near-term catalyst for negative policy. UBS is watching the post-midterm policy backdrop, and higher valuations look warranted.
Favorable ISM Manufacturing readings support a cyclical manufacturing upcycle and the sector has exposure to secular themes.
Defensive ballast if growth slows. About 25% of the sector has material exposure to AI power demand.
Incentives to de-escalate the Middle East war outweigh re-escalation risk, which makes risk-reward less attractive.
Slower growth and a less constructive deregulation backdrop reduce support. Cut from Attractive.
Focus tech exposure on quality and reduce concentration.
Banks, industrials, IT, health care and utilities are preferred sectors in Europe.
Rising electricity demand from data centers and electrification. Forward P/E derated from 16.8x to 15.4x since February.
Weak Chinese demand for autos and luxury goods, which are about 60% of the sector by market cap.
Housing downturn, NIM pressure and softening credit quality. UBS stays cautious on housing-exposed segments.

earnings_insights: UBS CIO forecast: S&P 500 EPS USD 360 in 2026 (+29%) and USD 415 in 2027 (+15%), raised on stronger 3Q results. This is a UBS estimate, not a reported figure.
UBS CIO forecast: Eurozone earnings growth 20% in 2026, 15% in 2027, 8% in 2028. Q3 results showed revenues back to growth, margins recovering and unusually positive revisions.
UBS CIO forecast: UK earnings growth 24% in 2026, 6% in 2027, 4% in 2028. Energy accounts for 14-15pp of 2026 growth.
UBS CIO forecast: SMI profit growth 11% in 2026 and 8% in 2027. Over 90% of SMI profits come from abroad.
UBS CIO forecast: MSCI Asia ex-Japan earnings +72% in 2026 and +20% in 2027, MSCI EM +63% in 2026 and +20% in 2027, Topix +12% in FY26 and +10% in FY27.

Reported 3Q26 data via BofA: earnings growth for core US IG issuers (excluding financials, energy, tech/AI) was 9.4% y/y versus 7.7% in 2Q, and revenue growth was 6.8% y/y. Across all listed US IG issuers earnings growth was 25.5% y/y. Earnings beat expectations by 4.4% versus 8.2% in 2Q.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Hotter than expected. It pushed rate-hike expectations and long-term yields back above 5%.

macro_indicators.reading: 3.7%, from below 2% a few months ago
macro_indicators.interpretation: Sharp acceleration. UBS expects disinflation to resume gradually but may not show before 1Q27.
UBS expects a move toward 2.5% in 2027.
Private demand was strong. 4Q is tracking around 2%.

macro_indicators.reading: UBS forecasts 25bp hikes in December and March, with rates at 4.25-4.50% through 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS calls these recalibration hikes. Markets price about 75bps more by mid-2027, which UBS considers too hawkish.
Resilient consumption and German fiscal spending offset the energy drag.
UBS expects two more ECB hikes (December and March 2027) and easing from early 2028.

macro_indicators.reading: 1.5% y/y in October, highest since late 2023
macro_indicators.interpretation: Half the rise is energy. UBS expects 0.8% in 2027 and SNB hikes in March and June 2027 to 0.5%.
Healthy conditions. Swiss GDP grew 0.2% q/q in 3Q26.
Soft consumer demand and lower food and gold prices.
Driven by energy and tech-related goods.
Stronger investment partly offsets slower exports and property weakness.
UBS base case is USD 90 by June 2027 and USD 80 by December 2027.

macro_indicators.reading: -1.2% m/m in October, about -6.7% from the March 2026 peak
macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus now expects a 10-15% peak-to-trough fall after the RBA's latest hike.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold, with a December 2027 target of USD 5,000/oz
trade_ideas.rationale: Current prices, the target, a forward curve near USD 3,900 and vol around 25% offer an attractive risk-reward for a long.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher real yields and a firmer dollar could keep gold below USD 4,000 in the near term.

trade_ideas.description: Sell gold volatility as an indirect way to benefit from the positive gold outlook
trade_ideas.rationale: Benefits from the positive price view and requires willingness and capacity to take a long position if prices fall materially.
trade_ideas.risk: Forced long gold position if prices decline materially further.

trade_ideas.description: Add copper exposure during periods of weakness
trade_ideas.rationale: Electrification, power networks and data centers support demand, and long mine-development times constrain supply.

trade_ideas.description: Favor GBP and select EM carry (MXN, BRL, ZAR, INR). Use CHF as a funding currency for long currency-cross positions.
trade_ideas.rationale: GBP offers high carry with contained volatility and a hawkish BoE. EM currencies have improved valuations and positioning.
trade_ideas.risk: A longer or more aggressive Fed tightening cycle could extend USD strength and delay carry recovery.

trade_ideas.description: Own 2- to 5-year Treasuries, and extend toward 10 years selectively for diversification
trade_ideas.rationale: The 2-5 year segment has the best risk-reward given the tightening already priced in.
trade_ideas.risk: Hotter inflation could force more aggressive Fed hikes.

trade_ideas.description: Rebalance concentrated tech and single-stock positions into health care, industrials, utilities, US equal-weight and Eurozone equities
trade_ideas.rationale: Reduces concentration risk. Eurozone equities offer similar earnings growth to the US at lower valuations.
trade_ideas.risk: AI boom scenario where concentrated US tech leads.

risk_factors: AI bust (20% probability): AI stocks deflate because capacity growth outstrips demand, S&P 500 falls to 5,500 and MSCI ACWI to 1,000 by December 2027.
Yield reset (10% probability): persistent inflation forces further central bank hikes, 10y yield reaches 5.50%, S&P 500 falls to 7,000 and US growth slows to about 1% or below.
The AI capex outlook after 2027 and monetization pace, plus financing constraints, power and grid bottlenecks and possible AI regulation after the US midterms.
Persistent inflation and a Fed that hikes beyond the recalibration path, including a possible 50bp December move after Waller's comments.
Escalation in the Middle East, including disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, or a renewed energy shock.
Higher bond yields compress equity valuations. The Eurozone has the most visible tightening feedback.
Hyperscaler bond supply indigestion and widening spreads in AI-related and CCC credit.
Australian housing downturn and its lagged effect on consumption, the labor market and bank earnings.
Fiscal risks in Europe and French election uncertainty in 2027, plus possible US-EU tariff escalation.
charts_described: Chart on p.22 shows the change in price level from end February 2026 to end October 2026 for Brent crude, European natural gas, US gasoline, US diesel and EU gasoline. The text says Europe was hurt by gas prices and the US by diesel and gasoline.
Chart on p.23 shows the federal funds rate and the UBS CIO forecast against market pricing. The text says UBS expects two more Fed hikes followed by a hold.
vol_and_positioning: UBS expects shifting views on AI, debt, inflation and geopolitics to produce higher volatility. It recommends capital preservation strategies (including gold and copper), structured yield strategies that monetize volatility (including rates and oil), and predefined market-entry strategies.

UBS suggests selling gold volatility as an indirect way to benefit from its positive gold outlook. Gold implied vol is about 25%, and the seller needs the willingness and capacity to take a long gold position if prices fall further.
US rate volatility is elevated. The 10y Treasury yield has traded in a 50bps range since early October.
USD positioning is heavy and could amplify the adjustment once the narrative turns.
The top 10 S&P 500 companies are just under 40% of the index, and UBS recommends equal-weight US strategies to reduce concentration.
US HY distress ratio is 7.5% and EUR HY is 7.0% (end of October), skewed by CCC issuers.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict and the US-Iran war have disrupted energy flows. Brent is about 30% above pre-conflict levels, and the Strait of Hormuz is cited as a risk.
Russia-Ukraine conflict continues in the base case. A ceasefire is part of the Goldilocks scenario.
US effective tariff rate stays at 10-15% in the base case and falls below 10% in the bull case. Trading partner retaliation is a bear-case risk.
US midterm elections left Democrats with majorities in both houses of Congress, raising questions about AI regulation and data center buildout.
Europe's election cycle includes the French presidential election in April/May 2027, German state elections and a Spanish parliamentary election in November 2026.
Possible MSCI reclassification of Indonesia is an overhang for that market and its currency.
Japanese and US authorities may intervene on the yen as it nears intervention thresholds.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment rises from USD 1.0tr to USD 1.4tr in 2027, and demand measured by GPU prices, cloud growth and adoption stays strong. In the Goldilocks scenario (20%) the S&P 500 reaches 9,500.
tension_points.bear_case: AI revenues of under USD 200bn today would need to approach a couple of trillion by decade-end to justify the investment. In the AI bust scenario (20%) the S&P 500 falls to 5,500 and MSCI ACWI to 1,000.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A moderation in expected AI capex, or investor focus on capex cuts in 2028 and beyond. UBS says the key uncertainty is 2028 rather than 2027.

tension_points.theme: Fed hiking path and bond yields
tension_points.bull_case: Markets overprice hikes. UBS expects only 25bp hikes in December and March, with the 10y yield settling at 4.5-5.0% as tighter financial conditions cap yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Hot inflation could push the Fed beyond recalibration hikes. Waller flagged a possible 50bp move, and markets price about 75bps more by mid-2027. The Yield reset scenario (10%) takes the 10y to 5.50%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sequence of hot inflation prints that pushes the Fed beyond the base-case 25bp hikes in December and March, or a December 50bp move.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient US data, persistent inflation and further Fed tightening preserve the dollar's yield advantage, so EURUSD trades sideways into early 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Lower inflation, slower AI investment and a shift from hikes to cuts let the dollar weaken, with DXY below 100 and EURUSD above 1.15 later in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A shift in the Fed debate from tightening toward a pause and cuts, or a faster decline in US inflation or growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Structural demand, central bank buying and easing real yields should lift gold to USD 5,000/oz by December 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: High real yields and a firm dollar could keep gold below USD 4,000 in the near term, and the move could fully retrace to USD 3,500.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Above-potential US growth, persistent inflation and a hawkish Fed keeping real yields elevated.

theme_stances.key_argument: US equities were downgraded to Neutral because risk-reward is more balanced, with concentration and AI monetization uncertainty limiting upside.
theme_stances.evidence: we downgrade US equities from Attractive to Neutral

theme_stances.key_argument: The Eurozone offers similar earnings growth to the US at lower valuations and with less dependence on AI-linked companies.
theme_stances.evidence: The Eurozone remains Attractive and is less exposed to some of the AI-related risks

theme_stances.key_argument: Easing real yields and structural demand should lift gold to USD 5,000 by December 2027 despite near-term headwinds.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect structural demand to provide support around those levels

theme_stances.theme: bonds attractive despite hawkish central banks
theme_stances.key_argument: Elevated starting yields offer income cushion, and tighter financial conditions limit how high yields can rise.
theme_stances.evidence: bond markets appear to be finding an equilibrium
